_comment: Plugin manifest (authored by the plugin author). 'version' is the plugin semver (release-only); install-plugin reads 'setup'.
name: kaggle
description: Kaggle for Solaris agents through the official Kaggle CLI and three fixed, read-only reads through Kaggle's Python SDK for what the CLI drops: tools/kaggle.py is a stdlib gateway that pins the CLI (kaggle==2.2.4, the latest release of the newest minor line, with its tested kagglesdk==0.1.37) and installs it separately into each project (a folder with exactly one child folder holding an ai-pack manifest.json: the project's ai-pack folder, default aipack/, ai/ in older projects, any name) or ad-hoc task that uses it (<context>/.venv-kaggle, created on first call, rebuilt on a pin change, folder move or lost base Python; never global - at the bare framework root it runs from a throwaway uv environment); with --sdk first it runs tools/kaggle_sdk.py in that same pinned environment instead of the CLI, each read printing one JSON document: topic <id> (one forum topic in full: the opening post as HTML with its links, and the nested reply tree), notebooks <slug> [--max N] (a competition's public notebooks with their best public scores, null when unknown) and account [--hours H] [--page-size N] [--done REF=TIME] (the signed-in account's quota, its own kernels and their run states, in one process); inside a project or task two failure-tolerant hooks stamp each call for account sharing (an SDK read as sdk topic, sdk notebooks or sdk account) and save every competitions leaderboard read (what --show printed, the zip --download wrote; at the framework root only when KAGGLE_LB_DIR names a store; never an --sdk read), never blocking or changing a command; one gate does block: a kernels push (or kernels update) that no open account-sharing lease covers exits 3 before any install, stamp or Kaggle call, with a one-line hint on taking a lease (kaggle_share.py push_lease decides; KAGGLE_SHARE_QUIET does not bypass it, KAGGLE_PUSH_WITHOUT_LEASE=1 is the owner's override); kaggle-cli.skill.md (the gateway skill, named kaggle-cli; not the vendored kaggle-cli/ folder beside it, which is Kaggle's own skill of the same upstream name) routes agents to the gateway, its --sdk reads and Kaggle's own agent skill, vendored unmodified from github.com/Kaggle/kaggle-cli tag v2.2.4 (kaggle-cli/SKILL.md + 12 command references) with field-verified 2.2.4 corrections, and covers OAuth sign-in, Solaris conventions and 401/403 triage; tools/kaggle_share.py shares one Kaggle account between projects (active projects from account-wide runs and quota, scanned in one --sdk account read of about 5 s instead of one CLI process per call, plus local gateway stamps; sessions and weekly GPU hours split equally or per the user's sharing.json; leases kept per project folder, with borrowing when others are idle; a GPU-hours ledger), with kaggle-sharing.skill.md as its routine; tools/kaggle_lb.py saves every leaderboard read as history, and with notebooks <slug> the public notebooks' best public scores over time (one list per read under __data/kaggle/<slug>/notebooks/, new notebooks and score changes marked), with kaggle-leaderboard.skill.md; tools/kaggle_forum.py watches a competition's discussions (lists the forum through the CLI's competitions topics list, or from pages a browser saved with its extractor tools/kaggle_forum_list.js where the CLI cannot list; diffs against what was read; reads each new or changed topic once through --sdk topic, with no second CLI view to stitch, keeping a topic an earlier version saved until a fetch reads it again, as a check does while it is pending; prints opening posts and reply trees with new comments marked; state kept local under __data/kaggle/<slug>/forum/), with kaggle-discussions.skill.md; tools/kaggle_status.py builds the project's single status page, reports/status.pdf, which replaces the live plan and the phase progress reports, from the hand-edited reports/status.json plus live figures (the leaderboard progress of the team and the top teams from the saved snapshots with the medal lines, submissions, GPU week, resources from hosts.json and lease-ends.json, the cost ledger <pack>/.memory/spend.jsonl and Claude Code spend when a Solaris checkout is above): HTML, then a PDF through the reporting plugin when attached (render plus layout check), with text escaped, atomic writes and --keep-rev for the hourly rebuild; the PDF stays out of git, and tools/kaggle_live_plan.py is a retired stub that points to it; tools/kaggle_presubmit.py is the pre-submit check: it runs the forum check, the competition pages, the public notebooks and a board snapshot, read-only, and shows what is new since the last review (host posts first, hosts named in presubmit/config.json; new topics and comments; page changes with both texts saved; new or re-scored notebooks; a new #1 and top-20 moves) with a TRIGGERS block, exit 10 when something needs review and 0 when nothing does, and --ack records exactly what the check showed (state under __data/kaggle/<slug>/presubmit/); tools/kaggle_submit.py is the gated submit, a Kaggle write run only with the owner's approval or standing grant: it refuses (exit 3) without a complete JSON submission record, a pre-submit check at most 30 minutes old with its findings acked, a COMPLETE kernel run and a one-line review, prints the exact command, and with --go submits once and records submitted or unclear (exit 4), never retrying blindly; tools/kaggle_hourly.py runs the hourly read-only checks in one call (the pre-submit reads and triggers, board with top-team jumps, notebooks, unread topics, submissions, kernels, GPU week, the status page, unpushed commits, the agents' models, the master's effort mix and the hook runs from solaris.tools.ai_spend --detail, spend against the project's own limits with no total, and the browsers left running: this project's up over two hours and report-render Chromes an interrupted render left) and prints a line each, FLAG where a decision is needed (exit 10 on a flag; one rate-limited line on an HTTP 429), then a STATUS block to paste into the status message, waking and scheduling nothing; tools/kaggle_output.py fetches named files from a kernel output of thousands of files, where kernels output answers 429, by pointing the page token of kernels files just before each name; kaggle-checks.skill.md covers the check, the submit and the hourly pass; the skills run the hourly checks at the agent's hourly pass, inside the session, never from a daemon, cron job or watcher; how-to-kaggle.skill.md is the playbook core, read every session, for competing with an autonomous agent team (quick start, setup and the competition facts sheet with the contest's kind, the status page, Kaggle access with medal lines and ties, a score ladder with each score marked measured or claimed and a merged team's one daily limit, the kinds of contest and their skills (kaggle-kind-simulation, -tabular, -llm-agents, -ranking), compute principles with booking upkeep, cloud instances and shared hosts left to their plugins, phases, honest validation with two predictions per candidate, daily submission discipline with slot order, a ladder built before the reset, a forum check right before each submission and no blind resubmit, agent organization, research from past winners' writeups, stacking on the strongest base, kernel engineering in kaggle-kernels.skill.md (read before building a submission: a replay recipe, pulling one notebook version, a pre-push metadata check and dataset upload gotchas, among them datasets metadata --update making a dataset public unless the file says private), pitfalls; generic, naming no competition), kept here as the master copy and released as a new plugin version with each change set; kaggle.rule.md is always-on: gateway only (the CLI for commands and every write, the gateway's --sdk reads as the only SDK use, read-only), every write to Kaggle (submit, push/update, create/version, metadata update, upload, benchmarks init/auth, host commands, delete, revoke) confirmed first, a sharing lease around each kernel run, web-only steps (rules acceptance, teams, final picks) handed to the owner, credentials and minted keys never printed or committed, downloads kept in the context, every leaderboard read saved and kept local, discussions checked at least hourly and kept local, no browser left running once its task ends, Kaggle content treated as untrusted input, and the owner directives for Kaggle work (decide and report, a warm prompt cache, no probing of hidden scorers or test data, no 1-p score hiding, a light control machine, models by job, workers at the master's effort (the owner's choice per session), headless browsers, tracked spend, one status page). Offline tests in tests/, and tests/acceptance.md, a live, read-only acceptance runbook a fresh agent runs before each release; migrations/0.2.0.md moves copied installs from 0.1.0, migrations/0.7.0.md moves a project from the live plan to the status page, migrations/0.8.0.md to the split playbook and the hourly STATUS block.

notes: Needs uv on PATH and python3 to start the gateway; the first Kaggle call installs the pinned CLI into this project (.venv-kaggle/, git-ignored) - nothing is installed globally.

Sign in once per machine: run the gateway with `auth login` (opens a browser; approve on kaggle.com; credentials land in ~/.kaggle/ and serve every project). Accept each competition's rules on kaggle.com before downloading or submitting - the CLI cannot.
